A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SDFit, with matching methods and core experiments. Their text, equations, tables and figures support comparison. v1 ends after its references; v2 additionally contains readable supplementary Sections S.1-S.4.

before.justification: v1 reports original shape-reconstruction and image-alignment experiments on Pix3D and Pascal3D+, including quantitative results in Tables 1-2 and qualitative reconstructions.

after.justification: v2 retains original reconstruction and alignment results and adds occlusion experiments, runtime measurements and ground-truth module ablations in the main text and supplement.

M1.justification: The DIT shape prior, OpenShape retrieval, ControlNet/DINOv2 features, RANSAC/PnP initialization and render-and-compare objectives remain substantively unchanged. The supplement explains and evaluates existing components. Reduced decoration budgets change experimental settings without introducing a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v2 adds COMIC hand-object grasp reconstruction for box, bottle, camera, knife, mug and spray categories. It also introduces synthetic occlusion scenarios on Pix3D, covering 10%-60% of object bounding boxes. The original Pix3D and Pascal3D+ coverage remains.

E2.justification: v2 adds ZeroShape+Inpaint for occlusion comparisons and ground-truth shape/pose controls in S.3. OpenShape disappears from the unoccluded reconstruction comparison but remains as OpenShape+RnC in image alignment. SDFusion receives a chair/sofa aggregate in v2 Table 3, whereas v1 Table 1 reports chair results and sofa N/A.

E3.justification: v2 adds CLIP similarity evaluated using the highest score from five regularly sampled views and stops reporting F-Score at threshold 5. New protocols include controlled occlusion levels, ground-truth module substitutions, and decoration configurations varying views and diffusion steps (Table 2). The stated 300-plus-1000-iteration fitting schedule remains unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds occlusion sensitivity analysis (Figure 8 and S.2), decoration speed-accuracy sensitivity (Table 2), feature-matching examples (S.1), and ground-truth shape/pose ablations (S.3). These substantially extend v1's diagnostic evidence. The feat@T versus feat@Sinit comparison remains for alignment, but its unoccluded shape-reconstruction results are removed.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without uncertainty. v2 adds mean and standard deviation for occlusion results in Figure 8 and Table S.1, including uncertainty for the retained 0% reference results. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds, and v2 does not clearly explain the sampling basis of these deviations.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for occlusion, CLIP similarity, runtime and module ablations; for example, COMIC mean CD is 3.25 for SDFit versus 6.53 for ZeroShape (Table 1). Alignment scores are unchanged between v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 4. The unoccluded CD values 3.53 and 3.44 are averages of v1's SDFit and ZeroShape category scores, not performance gains. Per-category unoccluded results and F@5 entries disappear.

T1.justification: The SDF representation, fitting losses, geometric regularizer, retrieval rule and correspondence mathematics retain their substantive content despite notation and equation-order edits. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs. The added CLIP evaluation does not introduce a new formal derivation.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contributions on joint pose/shape fitting, initialization and generalization without retraining. v2 makes strong robustness to occlusions an explicit contribution and a central abstract, introduction and conclusion claim. This extends the scope beyond v1's qualitative discussion of recovering self-occluded parts.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations based on unoccluded geometric cues, semantic defects missed by Chamfer distance, and redundant decoration views accumulating noise. It presents learned methods as complementary and adds a finite-grid fine-detail limitation in S.4. v1's explanation of elongated sofas caused by camera/depth/normal errors is removed; its left-right ambiguity discussion is largely retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies diffusion-step counts and configuration-specific decoration timings in Table 2, while retaining the optimizer schedule, mesh-grid resolution and GPU information. It removes v1's explicit centering, padding and 224-by-224 downsampling paragraph; this establishes lost documentation, not changed preprocessing. Both versions still promise a future code release.

R1.justification: The related-work survey is largely retained. v2 adds targeted positioning against DDIT's point-cloud fitting and emphasizes its use of Diff3F without known object-part connectivity. New citations include CLIPScore, Inpaint Anything and Depth Pro; Point-Bind/Point-LLM, several human-regression references and headset references are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are substantially rewritten, and method exposition is broadly condensed and rephrased. The contribution list moves earlier, Section 4.3 becomes Evaluation, and new supplementary Sections S.1-S.4 reorganize explanation and discussion. Much of the original main-text Future Work paragraph is removed or recast.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figure 2, revises diagrams 3-5, and adds occlusion Figures 7-9, feature-matching Figure S.1 and new analysis tables. The wide per-category reconstruction table becomes a compact class-averaged table. Existing material is also relocated: v1 Figure 7 becomes v2 Figure 10, and Table 2 becomes Table 4.

improvement.justification: New synthetic and real occlusion tests, runtime sensitivity and ground-truth module ablations improve empirical support beyond v1's benchmark comparisons. The net gain is limited by lost per-category reconstruction and preprocessing detail, plus inconsistent new reporting: ZeroShape's CD at 50% occlusion is 7.01 in Figure 8 but 6.76 in Table S.1.
